headline: Avoid despite ~50% share price decline — earnings hard to forecast accurately and investors unlikely to trust guidance going forward
reasoning: Greg Lowe warns that a falling share price should not be mistaken for value. Harvey Norman is down circa 50% and looks cheap on earnings estimates, but those earnings are difficult to forecast accurately and investor willingness to trust future guidance is even harder to predict. He prefers to wait for an earnings bottom and at least six months of visible stability or growth before becoming interested.
quote: Just because the share price is down, do not mistake it for value. I'll repeat that again, just because the share price is down, do not mistake it for value. And when you look at companies like unfortunately Harvey Norman and JB Hi Fi, fantastic companies share prices down circa 50% and on a lot of earnings estimates, it does appear to be very, very cheap. But those companies, they can be cheap for a reason. It is very hard to forecast accurately where those earnings will come in. And then even harder to forecast is will investors actually believe the guidance going forward. So our perspective is to avoid these companies, as tempting as they might be.
episode_title: Greg warns cheap shares aren’t always value
